skill.name: ux-waiting-audit
skill.description: Audit web applications with long-running operations by guiding screenshot capture, browser state checks, checklist scoring, and prioritized waiting UX recommendations.
skill.summary: Evaluate loading states and progress feedback for operations that take 30 seconds or longer.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: The static URL, filesystem, external-command, and screen-upload findings are false positives caused by examples, Markdown syntax, and local screenshot workflow notes. No evidence found of prompt injection, command execution, or screenshot upload. A semantic risk remains because the skill asks users for login credentials during authenticated audits.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the request for login credentials with manual login, SSO handoff, or a scoped test account. State that users should not share passwords.
Add guidance to redact personal data, keep screenshots local, and delete report assets when no longer needed.
Require explicit user approval before coordinate clicks, form submissions, or triggering production operations.

content.user_title: Audit Waiting UX for Web Apps
content.value_statement: Long waits can make users think a web app is frozen or slow. This skill audits waiting states and turns observations into prioritized UX recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Guides browser-based screenshots at start, interval, and completion states.
Uses a 10-point checklist for progressive value, progress feedback, interruptions, and completion UX.
Provides JavaScript snippets for checking spinners, progress bars, status text, and result counts.
Structures findings with evidence, strengths, gaps, quick wins, and priority levels.
Compares observed patterns with common waiting UX examples from modern products.
limitations: Requires a browser automation tool and access to the target web application.
May expose sensitive screen content unless screenshots are redacted or handled locally.
Does not replace performance profiling, user research, or accessibility testing.
Needs clear user guidance for authenticated flows and destructive operations.

use_cases.title: Review Launch Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess whether a new long-running flow gives users enough progress, context, and control before release.

use_cases.title: Improve Long Task Feedback
use_cases.description: Find gaps in loading states, progress indicators, partial results, and completion moments for a key workflow.

use_cases.title: Document Waiting State Regressions
use_cases.description: Capture repeatable evidence when a slow operation loses status text, progress feedback, or cancellation options.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Public Demo
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of a visible web flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the waiting UX for [URL]. Focus on [operation]. Capture start, 10 second, 30 second, and completion states. Summarize the top three improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Waiting Flows
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison across related product flows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare waiting states for [flow A] and [flow B] in [product]. Score each against the checklist and identify shared quick wins.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Authenticated Report Generation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit using a safe authenticated session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [authenticated app] using a test account or manual login. Trigger [operation], document each waiting state, and recommend production-safe improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Prioritized UX Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report for product and engineering planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full waiting state audit for [product area]. Include screenshot evidence, checklist scoring, severity, implementation effort, and a P1 to P3 roadmap.

output_examples.input: Audit a report generation flow that takes about 45 seconds.
output: Overall score: 5 of 10 waiting UX categories are addressed.
P1: Add status text that explains what the system is doing.
P2: Show partial results before the final report is ready.

output_examples.input: Compare search and export waiting states in a SaaS dashboard.
output: Search gives immediate partial results, while export shows only a spinner.
Add progress percentage and file count to the export flow.
Keep users in the dashboard while the export continues.

output_examples.input: Review an AI agent workflow that runs for one minute.
output: The workflow explains the task but lacks time estimates and cancellation.
Add a heartbeat counter, recent activity log, and stop option.
Celebrate completion with a clear result summary and next action.

best_practices: Use test accounts and staging data when auditing authenticated products.
Capture the same flow at consistent intervals so evidence is comparable.
Pair screenshot observations with DOM checks before making recommendations.
anti_patterns: Auditing only the final screen and ignoring the waiting timeline.
Sharing production credentials or screenshots with personal data in the report.
Treating every spinner as acceptable without checking status, progress, or cancellation.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits how web apps communicate progress during long-running operations, including spinners, status text, partial results, and completion states.

faq.question: Does it run performance tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on user-facing waiting experience, not backend timing, trace analysis, or load testing.

faq.question: Can it audit authenticated apps?
faq.answer: Yes, but use manual login or a scoped test account. Do not share production passwords in prompts.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It needs browser automation that can open pages, take screenshots, and run simple page-state checks.

faq.question: What does the report include?
faq.answer: The report includes a timeline, checklist scores, evidence, critical gaps, quick wins, and prioritized recommendations.

faq.question: Is it only for AI products?
faq.answer: No. It is useful for exports, searches, reports, deployments, uploads, and any operation with visible waiting time.
